inspection_outcome: One bounded source-to-claim overstatement; remaining declared scope unchanged

findings.claim_location: Section 2.6 p.6, ongoing image-misclassification example; prior report Section 4.
findings.claim_fidelity: The source literally asserts that the misclassification is still occurring more than eight years later. The predecessor report softened this into a claim that a longstanding problem persists. The proposed revision restores the literal claim and distinguishes its stronger temporal inference from the cited observations.
findings.checked_citation_excerpt: Appelman describes the 2015 Google mislabelling and the 2021 Facebook 'primates' incident, then says that Google and Apple failed to provide any search results for gorillas in the later 44-image test and reports disabled primate search as the likely explanation.
findings.operative_assumptions: This is a source-to-claim comparison of the cited 2023 account, not a claim that all deployed classifiers were tested or that no later misclassification occurred. Exact NYT full-text/test artifacts were not independently acquired.
findings.decisive_evidence: The source p.6 assertion is about recurring harmful outputs; the saved 2023 account's new observation is suppression/no returned results. Suppression documents an unresolved capability/workaround problem, but it does not entail the asserted contemporaneous recurrence.
findings.dependency: This affects one historical illustration supporting the neglect/exclusion discussion. The six-trap argument, specificity/pluralism/inclusion recommendations and the paper's own defeasible alternatives do not require this particular claim of fresh recurrence. The bounded evidence overstatement supports Minor, while actual 2023 recurrence remains Needs Evidence.
findings.counterevidence: The most charitable reading is persistence of an unresolved recognition limitation; the workaround and earlier incidents support that narrower concern. They do not justify silently changing what the paper's literal sentence says. This finding does not prove the underlying bias was fixed.
findings.correction_scope: Describe the 2015/2021 incidents and the 2023 restricted-search workaround separately; do not characterize the 2023 test as observing fresh harmful labels.
findings.source_claim_normalized_excerpt: mistaking Black people for gorillas ... is still occurring more than 8 years after the problem was first identified

findings.claim_location: The actual occurrence and frequency of fresh harmful image labels in 2023.
findings.decisive_evidence: The inspected source does not provide the required direct output observations. The full primary test record has not been independently inspected.
findings.dependency: Do not transform the documented citation overstatement into a proof that recurrence was false.
findings.counterevidence: Earlier incidents and continued suppression justify concern but leave this empirical question open.
findings.correction_scope: Direct contemporaneous output evidence would be needed to resolve recurrence.
